explain.say: Right at the bottom is the trench. The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest place on Earth, about 11,000 metres deep at a spot called Challenger Deep. If you dropped Mount Everest in, its top would still be about 2 kilometres under water!

faq.q: How deep is the Challenger Deep?
faq.a: About 10,900 to 11,000 metres below the sea surface. It is the deepest known point in the Mariana Trench and in all the oceans.
asks: What is the deepest point in the ocean?

faq.q: Has anyone been to the bottom of the Mariana Trench?
faq.a: Yes. Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh went down in 1960 in a submarine called Trieste. James Cameron went alone in 2012, and Victor Vescovo dived several times from 2019.
asks: Who went to the deepest part of the ocean?

faq.q: Why is the deep sea dark?
faq.a: Water soaks up sunlight. Below about 1,000 metres no sunlight is left at all, so it is completely dark.
asks: Where does the light go in the ocean?

faq.q: Could Everest fit in the Mariana Trench?
faq.a: Yes. Everest is 8,849 metres tall and the trench is about 11,000 metres deep, so Everest's top would still be about 2 kilometres under water.
asks: Is the Mariana Trench deeper than Everest is tall?

faq.q: Does anything live at the bottom of the trench?
faq.a: Yes. Tiny shrimp-like animals called amphipods, sea cucumbers and microbes live there, even under huge water pressure, more than 1,000 times the air pressure you feel.
asks: What lives in the Mariana Trench?

facts: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 10,900 to 11,000 metres deep, the deepest known point in the ocean.
Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh reached the Challenger Deep in the bathyscaphe Trieste in 1960.
